record.paper_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
record.original_question: Let Γ be a closed Jordan curve in the extended plane, and suppose that ∞ ∈ Γ. Let f1 , f2 map the upper and lower half-planes, respectively, onto the two different domains in C bounded by Γ, with f1 (∞) = f2 (∞) = ∞. Then, if h = f2−1 ◦f2 , h is a homeomorphism of R onto R. It is known that Γ is a quasi-circle if and only if h is quasi-symmetric (that is, there exists a constant c such that 1 h(x + t) − h(x) ≤ ≤c c h(x) − h(x − t) for all x, t ∈ R). Can one characterise the function h for general Jordan curves Γ? In particular, can every function h : R → R be generated in this fashion? (L. Bers; communicated by A. Baernstein II)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let Γ be a closed Jordan curve in the extended complex plane $\widehat{\mathbb{C}} = \mathbb{C} \cup \{\infty\}$ with $\infty \in \Gamma$. Then Γ separates $\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$ into two complementary Jordan domains $D_1, D_2$. Let $f_1$ map the upper half-plane $\mathbb{H}^+$ conformally onto $D_1$ and $f_2$ map the lower half-plane $\mathbb{H}^-$ conformally onto $D_2$, normalized so that $f_1(\infty) = f_2(\infty) = \infty$. By Carathéodory's theorem, each $f_i$ extends to a homeomorphism of the closed half-plane onto $\overline{D_i}$, and the welding homeomorphism $h := f_2^{-1} \circ f_1 : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a well-defined orientation-preserving homeomorphism of the real line.

It is classical that Γ is a quasi-circle if and only if $h$ is quasi-symmetric, i.e. there exists a constant $c \geq 1$ such that
$$\frac{1}{c} \leq \frac{h(x+t) - h(x)}{h(x) - h(x-t)} \leq c$$
for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$ and all $t > 0$.

(a) Give an intrinsic characterization of the homeomorphisms $h : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ that arise as conformal weldings of closed Jordan curves Γ in $\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$ through $\infty$.

(b) In particular, determine whether every orientation-preserving homeomorphism $h : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ can be realized in this fashion as a welding homeomorphism of some such Jordan curve Γ.
artifact.status_search_result: The general characterization problem of conformal welding homeomorphisms is a long-standing open question. Substantial partial progress is known: quasi-symmetric maps correspond to quasi-circles (Beurling–Ahlfors), and Bishop (Annals of Math, 2007) characterized weldings of "flexible" curves as the log-singular homeomorphisms. Not every orientation-preserving homeomorphism is a welding, but every homeomorphism is a welding in weaker senses (e.g. recent work showing every circle homeomorphism is a composition of two weldings, arXiv:2501.06347). A complete intrinsic characterization remains open.

status_evidence.title: Conformal welding and Koebe's theorem (Bishop)
status_evidence.snippet: An orientation-preserving homeomorphism h of the circle is the conformal welding of a flexible curve iff it is log-singular.
status_evidence.claim: Bishop gave a characterization of weldings of flexible Jordan curves, indicating partial progress.

status_evidence.title: Every circle homeomorphism is the composition of two weldings
status_evidence.snippet: Every orientation-preserving circle homeomorphism is a composition of two welding homeomorphisms.
status_evidence.claim: Recent partial result; not every homeomorphism is itself a welding, but every one is a composition of two.

status_evidence.title: On conformal welding homeomorphisms associated to Jordan curves
status_evidence.snippet: Studies which homeomorphisms arise as weldings of Jordan curves.
status_evidence.claim: Active investigation of the welding characterization problem indicates it is not fully resolved.
